overview: This table helps decide which group of battle voice lines plays when a character attacks, uses Cursed Energy, or reacts.
description: One row is a 13-slot, action/situation-indexed bundle of VoiceGroupDataTable IDs for one character voice variant. A CharacterVoiceGroupSetDataTable field selects the row; PlayVoice selects one slot by voice Kind/Index, and the resolved VoiceGroup row runs the actual random voice-candidate lottery into VoiceDataTable cues.

Id.simple: The name the game uses to find this set of voice lines for a character's action or reaction.
Id.technical: FName primary key (export column ID, ImportKeyField=Id). CharacterVoiceGroupSetDataTable's action/situation FName fields - for example Id_CharacterVoiceGroup_NormalAttack1, Id_CharacterVoiceGroup_CursedEnergyAttack1_2 and Id_CharacterVoiceGroup_ExtraAttack1 - and the generic PlayVoice cases resolve this Id with Action_FindCharacterVoiceGroupRow over DTM.CharacterVoiceGroupDataTables (+0x530). The finder rejects None when bCheckNone=true and returns the first typed FindRow hit in table order; every reconstructed call site passes true, while CP_230's inline walk checks IsNone() explicitly. The constructor declares no special Id default, so an unset FName is NAME_None.

Id_VoiceGroup.simple: The ordered voice groups the game can choose from for this action or reaction. The current attack step or situation decides which one plays, and blank places mean no voice plays.
Id_VoiceGroup.technical: TArray<FName>. A group row comes either from the active attack action's virtual GetVoiceGroupRow (Kind 2) or from a generic PlayVoice set field; the chosen element is Id_VoiceGroup[Index] for Kinds 1/4/5/8/9/10, Id_VoiceGroup[Index-1] for Kinds 3/6/7 (which require Index>0), and Id_VoiceGroup[Index==0 ? GetAttackVoiceIndex() : Index] for Kind 2 (a negative fallback is rejected). The selected FName is resolved through ActionController_FindVoiceGroupRow over DTM.VoiceGroupDataTables (+0x750). No bounds check is applied at any read site; NAME_None is rejected by the finder/typed FindRow even though Kind 2 passes bCheckNone=false. The constructor adds no entries or default IDs: all 2,460 exported rows have exactly 13 slots, and 25,372 of their 31,980 slots are literal 'None' unused filler.

notes: At boot the manager creates a FPrimaryAssetId of type 'DataTable' and name CharacterVoiceGroupDataTable from the shipped AssetManager scan, resolves it to a UDataTable, and appends it to DTM.CharacterVoiceGroupDataTables (+0x530). Action_FindCharacterVoiceGroupRow walks that array in order and returns the first hit; Unreal's typed UDataTable::FindRow itself checks that RowStruct is a child of FGameDataTableRow_CharacterVoiceGroup and rejects NAME_None, so the finder needs no separate struct test. The 45 per-character JSON shards all carry the same Name, are a partition of the rows, and are export views rather than 45 runtime tables; their union exactly equals the 2,460-row master export.

Indirect selection chain: character setup caches a CharacterSoundDataTable row (AGameCharacter +0x3D0); its Id_CharacterVoiceGroupSet is an ordered candidate array. FindCharacterVoiceGroupSetRow(Mode) uses candidate 0 for mode 0, the saved NormalAttackVoiceIndex for mode 1, CursedEnergyAttackVoiceIndex for mode 2 and candidate 3 for low-HP mode 3, with bounds and None checks, then resolves the first matching CharacterVoiceGroupSet row. CP_051's passive buff overrides candidate IDs with CP_051_2/TYPEA_2/TYPEB_2/PINCH_2. The selected set field resolves this table; this table's selected slot then joins VoiceGroupDataTable.Id_Voice, whose entries join VoiceDataTable cues.

Consumer gating and precedence: the generic character route through AGameCharacter::GAISlot186 requires both bActionVoiceEnabled and bVoiceGroupPlaybackEnabled; direct action/controller PlayVoice calls bypass that wrapper. In PlayVoice, Kind 2's set mode comes from the active action's GetAttackVoiceGroupSetMode, and the low-HP mode-3 override can replace it except for Kind 1; Kind 4 applies that override only at Index==2 and Kind 5 only at Index 2/5/6. A qualified secondary target can rewrite Kind 2/3 requests with bSituationCheck into Kind 4 before any lookup.

Kind-to-field mapping for this row's upstream selector is Kind 1 DefaultAction, Kind 2 the Attack action's virtual GetVoiceGroupRow, Kind 3 Attack, Kind 4 SituationAttack, Kind 5 System, Kind 6 Damage1, Kind 7 SpecialDamage, Kind 8 Down, Kind 9 Guard and Kind 10 Unique. Normal/cursed-energy/super-attack actions choose their own set fields (including the cursed-energy level), and CN_140, CN_230, CP_020, CP_050, CP_070, CP_110, CP_120, CP_200 and CP_230 character actions override the virtual selector. The base FGameCharacterAction::GetVoiceGroupRow returns nullptr, so Kind 2 on an action without an override plays nothing.

This table selects a VoiceGroup row, not an individual cue. PlayVoice filters None out of that row's Id_Voice array, removes the last played ID when at least two candidates remain, picks uniformly from GameManager's studio random stream, resolves a VoiceDataTable row and calls PlayVoiceCue with its cue sheet/name; voice priority and history state can still suppress the result. No timing, distance or other numeric unit is stored in this table; Index is an array index whose zero/one-based convention depends on Kind.

Export checks: every one of the 2,460 rows has key == ID, exactly the two declared fields, and a 13-element TArray; 6,608 non-None entries reference 4,784 distinct VoiceGroupDataTable rows. Ten entries in ten rows name nine absent VoiceGroup rows (CN_040_BREAKFALL_01 in two Down rows and eight CP_230 CursedEnergyAttack2_* names). Conversely, eight non-None CharacterVoiceGroupSet extra-attack IDs for CP_250, CP_260, CN_122 and CN_250 have no row here, and nine group rows (CP_070/CP_081 variants) are unreferenced by the exported set fields. No reconstructed C++ reader was found for those four characters' extra-attack fields, so these are export/evidence gaps, not established retail behavior.

Native consumer evidence comes from the current Reconstruction sources with inline retail RVA annotations; no retail Blueprint graphs were reviewed, so Blueprint-only consumers cannot be excluded. Export row counts and cross-table references establish data relationships in the supplied snapshot but cannot prove retail completeness.

usages.detail: Shipped AssetManager config scans /Game/DataTables as PrimaryAssetType DataTable, which makes the named table loadable.
Typed first-match finder for CharacterVoiceGroup rows; rejects None when requested.
Selects a CharacterVoiceGroupSet row by variant/low-HP mode, which supplies the Id looked up here.
Reads the cached CharacterSound row's Id_CharacterVoiceGroupSet candidate list.
CP_051 passive swaps the candidate set IDs to alternate rows, changing which row here is reached.
PlayVoice applies situation/low-HP rewrites, maps Kind to a set field and defines the Id_VoiceGroup index convention.
Kind 2 asks the active Attack action for its CharacterVoiceGroup row.
Normal and air attack actions choose normal-attack fields from the set.
Cursed-energy and super attack classes choose level-specific or super fields from the set.
Character-specific extra-attack overrides choose their own set fields.
CP_230 bypasses the shared finder with an inline None-checked table walk for CursedEnergyAttack2_1.
Resolves the selected Id_VoiceGroup entry to a VoiceGroup row.
Builds the downstream non-None voice candidate list and random lottery from the resolved VoiceGroup row.
